task2_zero_iterations.reason_compiler_cannot_tell: the only static information is the node types of the two bounds (AST_NUM or not); no constant propagation for locals, no range analysis, no knowledge of a collection's length; no existing refusal for a provably-empty loop; no warning machinery (the only warning is the R111 deprecation warning); a runtime rule would break the 0-to-n-1 idiom (0 tak -1 would run twice); Claude's stated reason for not changing it is right
task2_zero_iterations.view: document, do not refuse: a refusal would refuse a legal, common, correct program (0-to-n-1 with n = 0); a refusal cannot say anything teachable because the compiler cannot know which case the student meant; the R126/R82 doors refuse programs that are never right, and a chakra with start > end is sometimes right; the documentation must state the rule, name the failure, and correct the books' Descending Loops sentence, which is the trap's carrier and is still uncorrected on v325 (English book :400)

title: every loop form, for the same defect; is zero iterations ever right; the discoverability finding; the two audit rows that are wrong

verdicts.task1: the language has exactly three loop forms; chakra counts down only when both ends are written as numbers and otherwise counts up, running zero times silently when the start is past a variable end (the trap is symmetric); yavat runs zero times on a false condition and that is correct; kuru cannot run zero times; krama/agrim cannot cause zero passes (a stray krama outside a loop is a silent no-op); no step form exists
verdicts.task2: zero iterations are legitimately right for yavat and for the 0-to-n-1 chakra over an empty collection; the compiler cannot tell the legitimate empty case from the broken countdown, so the right answer is documentation, not refusal — with the books' Descending Loops sentence fixed, because that sentence is what teaches the trap (and it is still uncorrected on v325)
verdicts.task3: the three-line program does not exist anywhere in the tree; varna_tak_ank is undiscoverable on main and on v325 (0 hits in either book, no reference row) and takes a mala of codes rather than a string; the honest program is 14 lines and needs seven untaught pieces (six on v325); v325 adds the section 4d table, the book section, and three examples, but no converter despite its handoff title
verdicts.task4: Claude is right on R19 (the empty-string sentence is true in its stated scope) and his is the fuller account on R18 (the braces section is not merely obsolete, its rule is false and its verified failure is the missing-mukhya error, stale since v265-v267); the changelog dispute also goes his way
